name: Cardiac Amyloidosis AL Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for AL Amyloidosis

criteria.description: Demonstration of amyloid deposits by Congo red staining with apple-green birefringence under polarized light
Evidence of monoclonal light chain (kappa or lambda) in serum or urine by immunofixation or free light chain assay
Cardiac involvement demonstrated by echocardiographic features of restrictive cardiomyopathy or cardiac MRI showing characteristic late gadolinium enhancement
Presence of clonal plasma cells in bone marrow biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of amyloid deposits with monoclonal light chain evidence and cardiac involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other amyloidosis types and confirmation of light chain origin

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic diastolic dysfunction with preserved ejection fraction
Disproportionate low QRS voltage relative to ventricular wall thickness

pathognomonic.symptomName: Amyloid deposits on Congo red staining

common.notes: Due to restrictive cardiomyopathy and heart failure
Due to autonomic neuropathy or cardiac dysfunction

occasional.notes: Due to amyloid deposition in flexor retinaculum

rare.notes: Secondary to heart failure or amyloid involvement

laboratory: Elevated serum free light chains with abnormal kappa/lambda ratio
Presence of monoclonal protein on serum or urine immunofixation
Elevated NT-proBNP and troponin levels indicating cardiac involvement
imaging: Echocardiography showing thickened ventricular walls with restrictive filling pattern
Cardiac MRI demonstrating diffuse late gadolinium enhancement
Technetium-99m pyrophosphate scan negative or low uptake (helps differentiate from ATTR amyloidosis)
genetic: No known germline mutations; somatic plasma cell dyscrasia
other: Bone marrow biopsy showing clonal plasma cell population

redFlags: Rapidly progressive heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Disproportionate low voltage ECG despite ventricular hypertrophy
Presence of monoclonal light chains in serum or urine
references: Merlini G, Bellotti V. Molecular mechanisms of amyloidosis. N Engl J Med. 2003;349(6):583-596.
Ruberg FL, Berk JL. Transthyretin (TTR) cardiac amyloidosis. Circulation. 2012;126(10):1286-1300.
Dispenzieri A, Gertz MA. Light-chain (AL) amyloidosis: diagnosis and treatment. Clin J Am Soc Nephrol. 2006;1(6):1331-1341.
